output.summary: The diff changes the upper-bound check in inBounds from `index < length` to `index <= length`, which violates the documented contract that valid integer indices are 0 through length-1. The changed source was read and confirms line 2 now reads `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. This makes the out-of-bounds index `length` report as in bounds, and makes an empty collection (length=0) report index 0 as valid, contradicting 'Empty collections have no valid index.' This is a correctness regression in a public function contract.

findings.title: inBounds accepts out-of-range index equal to length
findings.body: The change from `index < length` to `index <= length` breaks the documented contract that valid integer indices are 0 through length-1. With the new code, inBounds(length, length) returns true even though index length is out of bounds. For length=0, inBounds(0, 0) also returns true, violating the rule that empty collections have no valid index. Any caller relying on this predicate to guard indexed access will now be allowed to access one past the last element.
findings.evidence: Current source line 2: `return index >= 0 && index <= length;`. Diff shows the previous `index >= 0 && index < length` was replaced with `<=`. Contract states valid indices are 0 through length-1 and empty collections have no valid index.
findings.suggestion: Restore the strict comparison: `return index >= 0 && index < length;`
